title: The higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture
main_claim: For every fixed d>=3 there is c_d>0 such that every set of n>=2 points in R^d determines at least c_d n^{2/d} distinct distances. The proof is by contradiction in the least failing dimension, with a constant-factor (not n^{-o(1)}) loss.
coverage:
Read the whole of reduction.tex (Sec. 2) and checked each step. (1) Flat caps. (2) Prop red:directions: the rich-line discard sum; the greedy curve removal and the diagonal appeal to the sparse-cones theorem; the radius-class induction (L>=2M gives L^2/(2M) equal-distance pairs; the orthogonality identity; properness of the hyperplane section). The fiber count O(M^{2+(d-l)/2}) <= M^{d/2} holds for l>=4, and I checked the l<=3 cases. (3) Independent stars via the Hilbert lower bound and charging. (4) Edge count 2*sum s_rho^2 and Cauchy-Schwarz. (5) Rich-motion deletion, which costs o(N^4/M); pruning; min degree / A^{d-1} -> infinity. (6) Pair-flat/parameter identities and the polarization computations, both global ((v0-v0').(y0-y0') = (|p-p'|^2-|q-q'|^2)/4) and local (u_i.u_j = w_i.w_j). (7) Hypotheses (i), (ii), (a) and (b) of conc:theorem: e=d+1, r=d globally; e=d, r=d-1, h=d-2 locally. The isotropic caps are N <= A^{d-2} for d>=4, and for d=3 the survivor property. (8) The sampling/Chernoff/rank contradiction.

polynomial.tex: separators; socle/interpolation; the Hilbert upper and lower bounds and the rescaling H(bL) <= b^n H(L); the regularity-loss inequality; pooling; multiplicity compression, including the char-p degree arithmetic and the transfer to C; the projection-multiplicity formula; the polar bound.

secants.tex: the secant tangent lemma; generic depth with the Szemeredi-Trotter sum; terminal-curve deletion. For the latter I checked the line case (the parabolic-lift ST bound b*h_H <= CM^2; the Hoelder inequality T^3 <= L*sum((b/L)^{1/2} N_b^2)*(...)^2; the final O(N^2 M^2/A^2)), the d>=4 perspectivity/stabilizer count with its Cauchy-Schwarz step, and the d=3 valid-triple Hoelder argument with E = delta*N^{1/3}.

profiles.tex: the partition (thresholds, summability of discards, core E*L^2 = o(N)); budgets and rank propagation, including sum b_i = 0 and b_1+b_2 < 0; regularity; product testing; pair selection.

sparse-cones.tex and depth.tex:
- Retained products and image degree.
- Common-window label rank in all plateau cases. The comparison ratio min(A/(delta*D_d), A/(delta*D_1*D_2)) has no strict margin only when s = log B and b_d = 1.
- Outer-endpoint lift argument: e_j = B^{d-2k}; the bounds E*B^{2-c}/n <= sqrt(delta)*B^{-c} and E*M/n <= sqrt(delta)*M/A; the map-degree <= 1 argument via the local secant lemma.
- Separated-window margins b_1+b_{j+1}, -sum_{i>j+1} b_i and b_{j+1}-2, with the case coverage.
- Final narrow curve plateau: e_{d-1}/R = N/A against the exceptional degree delta*(N/A)*e^{-eta*s}.
- Depth: the narrow-window root count, e_j*B^{l+1}/N = R; the wide-window Sylvester rank drop plus compression, giving degree O(L^2/r) = B*e^{O(s)}.

motions.tex: Beck; effective planes; the general-type polynomial/null-flat derivative argument; planar type; the subdivision; line-image lemmas. I recomputed every exponent: b/m^{2/3} = (beta/4)*t^{9/14}; the non-line mass N^4/A * t^{-1/28}; nonparallel N^{8/3} t^{2/7} summing to N^{58/21}; parallel N^{19/6} t^{1/4} summing to N^{13/4}. Both are below N^{10/3}.

concentration.tex: the theorem statement, the separator lemma, the regularity lemma (start), the ACI statement, and the closing recurrence. I checked the barrier constants and the degree-comparison step.

Not verified line by line: the ruling-recovery lemma and the degree/exceptional-family proposition in concentration.tex (about lines 272-1015); most of approximation.tex; the classical-incidence appendix (ST, Guth-Katz higher richness, planar distances), which reproves standard results.
